title: BAGMAN AIInvocation
description: Canonical `AIInvocation` (CD-5 PID §26-30, WI-1). Durable, auditable record of one attempt to invoke a governed BAGMAN AI task against an authorised provider/capability. An `AIInvocation` is created the moment BAGMAN accepts a task request (status `REQUESTED`) and is durably updated as it moves through the deterministic state machine `ai.invocation.ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS` describes, until it reaches a terminal state (`SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, `REJECTED`). It is a provider-NEUTRAL result/provenance model (PID §70): nothing in this contract exposes raw Anthropic/LiteLLM response shapes. This contract never carries hidden chain-of-thought (PID §25) — only `output`/`confidence`/`validation_result`/`error_code`/`usage_metadata` and input/output provenance references. Every field this WI cannot yet populate (e.g. `prompt_contract_version`, `provider_model`, `output` before completion) is modelled as an explicitly-nullable, but always-REQUIRED, key — the same 'state the question, even if unanswered' doctrine `bagman.intake_record.v1` already uses — so a caller/reader can never confuse 'not yet known' with 'field omitted by accident'.

ai_invocation_id.description: Canonical BAGMAN identifier for this AI invocation (PID §26) — distinct from `evidence_id`, `intake_id`, `audit_event_id`, or any workflow ID.

task_id.description: Identifies the typed AI task requested (PID §21-22), e.g. `DOCUMENT_TYPE_PROPOSAL`. Deliberately OPEN (not a closed enum) so new tasks can be added without a contract redesign — the same doctrine `bagman.audit_event.v1`'s own `event_type` already uses. The actual closed set of tasks BAGMAN currently recognises is enforced in code by `ai.tasks.TASK_REGISTRY`, not by this schema.

task_version.description: Task contract version requested (PID §22/§31) — a task's input/output schema, prompt contract, and behaviour are versioned together; this pins which version this invocation was evaluated against.

role.description: Which of BAGMAN's two application-level provider-routing roles this invocation belongs to (PID §8/§20): `OPERATOR` (Claude, interactive) or `BACKGROUND` (routed via the existing Trinity LiteLLM installation using a BAGMAN-specific alias, PID §9). Closed enum — CD-5's locked three-tier topology (PID §2) recognises exactly these two application-level roles; the Mac-mini-vs-Trinity-escalation distinction within `BACKGROUND` lives entirely in `capability_alias`, never as a third value here.

provider.description: The BAGMAN provider ADAPTER that served this invocation (PID §27) — never the physical backend/model. Closed set of exactly the two adapters CD-5 authorises (PID §6/§8): `LITELLM` (the one existing Trinity LiteLLM installation, serving every `BACKGROUND` invocation regardless of whether the alias resolves to the dedicated Mac mini or to Trinity compute) and `ANTHROPIC` (the Claude operator provider). A closed enum here is a deliberate first line of defence against the raw-model-name-lockdown concern PID §5/§10 raises — this field can never become a place a caller injects an arbitrary provider or physical model identity.

capability_alias.description: For a `BACKGROUND` invocation: the exact BAGMAN-specific LiteLLM alias requested (PID §9) — always one of the closed set `bagman-fast`/`bagman-core`/`bagman-deep`, NEVER a `trinity-*` alias and NEVER a raw/physical model name (PID §5/§10). For an `OPERATOR` invocation: always `null` — Claude is not reached via a LiteLLM alias at all (PID §8), so this field carries no meaning for that role; the Claude model actually used is instead recorded, audit-only, in `provider_model` (per BAGMAN_OPERATOR_MODEL configuration, PID §18). The `role`-conditioned `allOf`/`if`/`then` rules below enforce this cross-field correspondence structurally, not merely by convention.

provider_model.description: Physical model identity actually observed from the provider response, when available (PID §10/§24/§27) — e.g. a specific Claude checkpoint, or the physical Mac-mini/Trinity model LiteLLM reports having served the request. AUDIT-ONLY: nothing in `ai/` reads this field to make a routing decision — routing is decided entirely by `task_id`/`role`/`capability_alias` before any provider is ever called, so this field structurally cannot influence what gets called next. `null` until the provider responds (or if the provider never discloses this).

started_at.description: UTC timestamp at which this `AIInvocation` was created (the moment it entered `REQUESTED`) — analogous to `bagman.intake_record.v1`'s `received_at`, not the moment execution actually begins (`RUNNING`). Stamped once, at creation, so every invocation (even one that never leaves `REQUESTED`) has a deterministic value to order and page by (`started_at DESC`, PID §44/§45's own ordering doctrine, reused here).

completed_at.description: UTC timestamp at which this invocation reached a terminal state (`SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, or `REJECTED`). Required key, explicit `null` while the invocation is still `REQUESTED` or `RUNNING`.

status.description: Invocation lifecycle state (PID §28; `TIMED_OUT`/`CANCELLED` added by the CD-6 reliability delta, PID §100.14/§100.16). Closed enum — `ai.invocation.ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS` is the single source of truth for which transitions between these values are valid; see that module's docstring for the exact state machine, the documented distinction between `REJECTED` (never dispatched to a provider at all — a pre-flight policy/contract refusal) and `RUNNING -> FAILED` (a dispatched call that errored, or produced output that failed structured validation), and the further distinction of both from `TIMED_OUT` (BAGMAN's own bounded timeout fired — a live runner timeout, or the bounded stale-RUNNING recovery backstop discovering and closing out an abandoned row) and `CANCELLED` (an invocation explicitly cancelled by an operator action or a deliberate application-level decision, never a failure/timeout on its own).

correlation_id.description: Identifier shared with every audit event and canonical write belonging to the same workflow story this invocation is part of (PID §58), e.g. evidence registered -> AI invocation -> AI proposal. The same correlation doctrine `bagman.audit_event.v1.correlation_id` already establishes.

actor.description: Who/what caused this invocation to be requested (PID §14, reusing `core.actor`'s exact closed `actor_type` vocabulary rather than inventing a parallel one for AI invocations).

actor_type.description: Matches `bagman.audit_event.v1.actor_type` exactly — the same closed set `core.actor.ALL` enforces in code.

actor_id.description: Identifies the SPECIFIC actor, e.g. `"matt"`, `"bagman-agent"`, `"document-ai-panel"`. Must not be a generic literal such as `"system"` alone (same doctrine as `bagman.audit_event.v1.actor_id`).

input_references.description: Canonical references this invocation's input traces back to (PID §29) — e.g. `{"evidence_id": "..."}`, `{"evidence_id": "...", "intake_id": "..."}`, or (CD-6 reliability delta, PID §98/§100) `{"conversation_id": "..."}` for a genuinely contextless Ask BAGMAN turn with no document/intake/entity attached. Open object (genuinely free-form: different tasks reference different canonical objects) but never opaque/disconnected from source evidence — `ai.invocation.derive_primary_input_reference` requires at least one of a fixed, documented set of recognised reference keys (`evidence_id`, `intake_id`, `entity_id`, `conversation_id`, in that precedence order — `conversation_id` deliberately last, see that function's own module docstring) to be present, both to satisfy PID §29 and to identify the subject the one-active-invocation concurrency guard (PID §73) applies to.

prompt_contract_version.description: Version identifier of the versioned prompt template/contract actually used for this invocation (PID §31), e.g. `"v1"` referencing `ai/prompts/document_type/v1.*`. WI-1 defines this field's shape only — no prompt CONTENT is authored by WI-1 (that is WI-2/WI-3 scope) — so every WI-1-created invocation carries `null` here; a later work item's provider adapter populates it once it actually renders and sends a versioned prompt.

output.description: The structured proposal the provider returned (PID §24/§30), exactly as validated/rejected by `validation_result` — never a free-text 'I think this appears to be...' string. `null` while `REQUESTED`/`RUNNING`, or when the invocation reached `REJECTED` before ever being dispatched. May be present (and preserved, per PID §76 'do not repair malformed output silently') even when `status` is `FAILED` due to a structured-validation failure — the raw non-conforming output is retained for audit, not discarded.

confidence.description: Task-specific confidence value (PID §55) — its MEANING is defined per-task by that task's own `confidence_policy` (`ai.tasks.TaskContract.confidence_policy`); this contract only pins its numeric shape (0-1), not a universal interpretation or threshold. `null` until produced.

validation_result.description: Result of validating `output` against the requested task's `output_schema` (PID §24/§76), produced by `ai.tasks.validate_task_output`. `null` until an output has actually been validated (or rejected before ever producing one).

error_code.description: Short machine-readable reason this invocation reached `FAILED` or `REJECTED` (PID §35), e.g. an `error_code` from `core.errors`, or a provider/task-specific code such as `TIMEOUT`. `null` unless the invocation is `FAILED` or `REJECTED`.

usage_metadata.description: Safe, non-sensitive usage information where available (PID §71) — e.g. input/output token counts, provider request ID. Never provider billing/cost truth (that remains outside BAGMAN's canonical model). Open object, defaults to `{}` until populated.

latency_ms.description: Observed provider call latency in milliseconds (PID §71), when available. `null` until measured.

schema_version.description: Contract version identifier for this AIInvocation. Must literally equal `"bagman.ai_invocation.v1"` for instances of this schema version.
